s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Change of State
s.d: to change to a previous good state
s.g: to restore; to cause again to be; restoration
s.c: A rendering of ἀποκαθίστημι in ⟦Mark 3:5|Mark 3:5⟧ as was healed is justified on the basis that at a previous time the hand was crippled, but ἀποκαθίστημι in and of itself does not mean to be healed. Note, however, a contrasting situation in ἰάομαι (LN 13.66).

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to send someone back to a place where one has been before
s.g: to send back; to cause to go back

s.dp: Know › Well Known, Clearly Shown, Revealed
s.d: (figurative extension of meaning of ἀποκαλύπτω ‘to uncover, to take out of hiding,’ not occurring in the NT) to cause something to be fully known
s.g: to reveal; to disclose; to make fully known; revelation

s.dp: Know › Well Known, Clearly Shown, Revealed
s.d: (figurative extension of meaning of ἀποκάλυψις ‘to uncover, to take out of hiding,’ not occurring in the NT) to cause something to be fully known
s.g: to reveal; to disclose; to make fully known; revelation

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Hope, Look Forward To
s.d: that which one looks forward to with eagerness and desire
s.g: what one eagerly expects; eager expectancy; eager desire
s.c: In ⟦Romans 8:19|Romans 8:19⟧ (see LN 25.63) ἀποκαραδοκία serves in some respects to reinforce the meaning of ἀπεκδέχομαι, but it appears to add a significant component of desire.

s.d: to reestablish proper friendly interpersonal relations after these have been disrupted or broken (the componential features of this series of meanings involve (1) disruption of friendly relations because of (2) presumed or real provocation (3) overt behavior designed to remove hostility, and (4) restoration of original friendly relations){N:001}
s.g: to reconcile; to make things right with one another; reconciliation
s.c: Because of the variety and complexity of the components involved in reconciliation, it is often necessary to use an entire phrase in order to communicate satisfactorily the meanings of the terms in this subdomain. In some languages, however, reconciliation is often spoken of in idiomatic terms, for example, ‘to cause to become friends again,’ ‘to cause to snap fingers again’ (a symbol of friendly interpersonal relations in many parts of Africa), ‘to cause to be one again,’ or ‘to take away the separation.’ A particularly crucial element in terms for reconciliation is the assigning of responsibility for original guilt in causing the estrangement. Some terms, for example, imply that the individual who initiates reconciliation is by doing so admitting his guilt in causing the estrangement. This, of course, provides a completely untenable meaning for reconciliation in speaking of God reconciling people to himself through Christ.|In a number of languages the contextual basis for an expression for reconciliation is often found in terms relating to the reconciliation of husbands and wives. Such expressions fit in well with many contexts in the Scriptures, especially in speaking of reconciliation of people to God, since God is frequently referred to as the husband and the believers as the wife.

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Change of State
s.d: to change to a previous good state
s.g: to restore; to cause again to be; restoration

s.d: to put something away for safekeeping
s.g: to store; to put away in a place

s.d: to exist, with the implication of having been established and thus having continuity and purpose
s.g: to exist; to exist for; to be set
s.c: In ⟦Colossians 1:5|Colossians 1:5⟧ the hope is the hope for reality, not a mere human feeling.

s.d: to be necessary in view of something being inevitable
s.g: to be necessary; must

s.d: to kill by beheading, normally an act of capital punishment
s.g: to cut the head off; to behead

s.d: to close off an area, and in the process of doing so, to exclude
s.g: to close off; to shut

s.d: to cut in such a way as to cause separation
s.g: to cut down; to cut off; to cut in two

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Judge, Condemn, Acquit
s.d: an official decision, frequently involving a legal verdict
s.g: decision; verdict
s.c: In ⟦2 Corinthians 1:9|2 Corinthians 1:9⟧ ἀπόκριμα is used figuratively; no actual official decision had been made, but in view of all of the difficulties which Paul and his colleagues had suffered, it seemed as though such an official decision had been rendered.

s.d: to respond to a question asking for information
s.g: to answer; to reply

s.d: to introduce or continue a somewhat formal discourse (occurring regularly with {L:λέγω<SDBG:λέγω:000000>}[a] ‘to say,’ {D:33.69}){N:001}
s.g: to speak; to declare; to say
s.c: A literal translation such as ‘at that time Jesus spoke and said’ (⟦Matthew 11:25|Matthew 11:25⟧) may sound redundant in many languages.

s.d: (derivative of {L:ἀποκρίνομαι<SDBG:ἀποκρίνομαι:000000>}[a] ‘to reply,’ {D:33.184}) that which is said in response to a question
s.g: answer; reply

s.dp: Know › Not Able To Be Known, Secret
s.d: to cause something to remain unknown, with the implication of concealment and inaccessibility{N:001}
s.g: to keep secret; to conceal
s.c: The passive expression ‘concealed’ may be rendered in an active form as ‘God has kept people from knowing about this wisdom.’

s.dp: Know › Not Able To Be Known, Secret
s.d: pertaining to not being able to be known and thus secret, possibly in view of something being separate
s.g: secret; not able to be known
s.c: The triple negation in ⟦Luke 8:17|Luke 8:17⟧ may lead to some shift in a number of languages, for example, ‘everything which is secret now will be known.’

s.d: to cause someone’s death, normally by violent means, with or without intent and with or without legal justification{N:001}
s.g: to kill

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἀποκτείνω<SDBG:ἀποκτείνω:000000>}[a] ‘to kill,’ {D:20.61}) to cause a state to cease, with the implication of strong emphasis and forceful action
s.g: to do away with; to eliminate
s.c: In ⟦Ephesians 2:16|Ephesians 2:16⟧ there is a subtle rhetorical device employed in ascribing to Christ the activity of ‘killing,’ when in reality he was the one who was killed on the cross in order to make life possible.

s.d: to cause a state, with focus upon the process
s.g: to cause; to give rise to; to give birth to

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἀποκυέω ‘to give birth to,’ not occurring in the NT) to be brought into being as something newly created
s.g: to bring into being; to cause to exist

s.d: to cause to roll away from a particular point
s.g: to cause to roll away; to roll away

s.d: to receive, with probable focus upon the source
s.g: to receive from; to obtain; to receive

s.d: to receive back something which one has previously possessed or its equivalent
s.g: to get back; to receive back; to be paid back

s.d: to lead or take away from a particular point
s.g: to lead off; to lead away; to take away; to take aside

s.d: to accept the presence of a person with friendliness{N:001}
s.g: to welcome; to receive; to accept; to have as a guest

s.d: to experience some event or state, often with the implication of something negatively valued{N:002}
s.g: to undergo; to experience

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Enjoy, Take Pleasure In, Be Fond of Doing
s.d: enjoyment based upon the satisfaction of one’s desires
s.g: enjoyment

s.dp: Existence in Space › Leave in a Place
s.d: to cause or permit something to remain in a place and to go away (with or without implying purpose)
s.g: to leave; to leave behind; to abandon

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to depart from a point definitively, with the possible implication of abandoning or deserting
s.g: to leave; to abandon; to desert

s.d: to leave it to someone to do something, with the implication of distancing oneself from the event
s.g: to let; to allow; to leave it to

s.d: to continue to exist, with the implication of being a part of a larger whole
s.g: to continue; to continue to exist

s.d: to destroy or to cause the destruction of persons, objects, or institutions
s.g: to ruin; to destroy; destruction
s.c: In a number of languages it is difficult to find a general term for ‘destruction.’ What has often happened is the extension of meaning from a more specific type of reference, for example, ‘to smash,’ to a more generic meaning of ‘to destroy,’ and whether one understands the specific or more generic meaning depends largely upon the context. Accordingly, in ⟦Acts 8:3|Acts 8:3⟧ one may find a figurative usage of a term meaning ‘to smash’ (though understood in a more generic sense), for example, ‘Saul then worked in order to smash the church.’

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Take, Obtain, Gain, Lose
s.d: to fail to obtain a valued object
s.g: to not obtain; to fail to get

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Take, Obtain, Gain, Lose
s.d: to lose something which one already possesses
s.g: to lose
s.c: ἀπόλλυμι in the sense of losing what one already possesses may be analyzed basically as ‘not to have that which one has previously had.’ There is, however, no suggestion in ἀπόλλυμι as to the particular type of circumstances involved in the loss, whether, for example, from neglect, by accident, or as the result of some external force.|It is also possible to interpret ἀπόλλυμι in ⟦Luke 15:8|Luke 15:8⟧ as ‘to not know where something is’ (see LN 27.29).

s.dp: Learn › Learn the Location of Something
s.d: to become unaware of the location of something{N:001}
s.g: to lose; to no longer know where something is
s.c: It is also possible to interpret ἀπόλλυμι in ⟦Luke 15:4|Luke 15:4⟧ as meaning a loss of possession (see LN 57.68)

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: an idiom, literally: to suffer the destruction of one’s life, or: to have one’s life destroyed
s.g: to experience the loss of life; to die
s.c: In ⟦Matthew 10:39|Matthew 10:39⟧ some scholars see in the use of ψυχή a reference not to physical life but to a particular quality of life. This is difficult to justify except in terms of the total context, and it may be that in ⟦Matthew 10:39|Matthew 10:39⟧ there is a degree of intentional ambiguity with respect to the meaning of ψυχή.

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: to die, with the implication of ruin and destruction
s.g: to die; to perish
s.c: It is possible to understand ἀπόλλυμαι in ⟦Luke 15:17|Luke 15:17⟧ as involving a measure of exaggeration.

s.d: to cease to exist, with a possible implication of violent means
s.g: to cease to exist; to no longer exist; to come to an end; to disappear

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Save in a Religious Sense
s.d: to be lost, in the religious or spiritual sense
s.g: to be lost; to perish

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the Greek name for the ruling angel in Hell; see {D:93.2}
s.g: Apollyon meaning Destroyer

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a city in Macedonia
s.g: Apollonia

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a Christian of Alexandria who worked in Ephesus and Corinth
s.g: Apollos

s.d: to speak on behalf of oneself or of others against accusations presumed to be false
s.g: to defend oneself

s.d: to speak on behalf of oneself or of others against accusations presumed to be false
s.g: to defend oneself

s.d: (derivative of {L:ἀπολογέομαι<SDBG:ἀπολογέομαι:000000>} ‘to defend oneself,’ {D:33.435}) the content of what is said in defense
s.g: defense; what is said in defense; how one defends oneself

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Holy, Pure
s.d: to cause a state of moral purity
s.g: to purify; to cause to be pure

s.d: to release or set free, with the implied analogy to the process of freeing a slave{N:001}
s.g: to set free; to liberate; to deliver; liberation; deliverance
s.c: In a number of languages one cannot speak of ‘being set free’ without specifying the particular manner or circumstances involved. In the case of ⟦Luke 24:21|Luke 24:21⟧, for example, it may be necessary to translate ‘to liberate Israel’ as ‘to cause Israel to be free from foreign control’ or ‘… from the power of Rome.’ A similar type of translation may be required in ⟦Luke 2:38|Luke 2:38⟧, but in the case of ⟦Ephesians 1:7|Ephesians 1:7⟧ it may be necessary to specify ‘we are set free from sin’ or ‘we are set free from our bad desires.’

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to cause (or permit) a person or persons to leave a particular location{N:001}
s.g: to let go away; to dismiss

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to cause someone to depart for a particular purpose
s.g: to send

s.d: to release from control, to set free (highly generic meaning applicable to a wide variety of circumstances, including confinement, political domination, sin, sickness){N:002}
s.g: to release; to set free

s.d: to dissolve the marriage bond
s.g: to divorce; to separate
s.c: Expressions for divorce are often based on terms meaning literally ‘to send away,’ ‘to separate from,’ or ‘to leave one another.’ However, in a number of languages idiomatic expressions are employed, for example ‘to send him off with his clothes,’ ‘to untie the knot between them,’ or ‘to throw away her hearthstones.’|Some persons have attempted to make an important distinction between ἀφίημι in ⟦1 Corinthians 7:11|1 Corinthians 7:11⟧ and χωρίζω in ⟦1 Corinthians 7:15|1 Corinthians 7:15⟧ on the assumption that ἀφίημι implies legal divorce, while χωρίζω only relates to separation. Such a distinction, however, seems to be quite artificial.

s.d: to remove the guilt resulting from wrongdoing
s.g: to pardon; to forgive; forgiveness
s.c: It is extremely important to note that the focus in the meanings of ἀφίημι, ἄφεσις, and ἀπολύω is upon the guilt of the wrongdoer and not upon the wrongdoing itself. The event of wrongdoing is not undone, but the guilt resulting from such an event is pardoned. To forgive, therefore, means essentially to remove the guilt resulting from wrongdoing.|Some languages make a clear distinction between guilt and sin, and terms for forgiveness are therefore related to guilt and not to the wrongdoing. Therefore, ‘to forgive sins’ is literally ‘to forgive guilt.’ Though terms for ‘forgiveness’ are often literally ‘to wipe out,’ ‘to blot out,’ or ‘to do away with,’ it is obviously not possible to blot out or to wipe out an event, but it is possible to remove or obliterate the guilt.

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to depart from a place or set of circumstances, with perhaps an implication of finality or significant separation or rupture being involved
s.g: to go away; to depart; to leave

s.d: to wipe off, as a means of getting rid of some adhering substance
s.g: to wipe off; to wipe away
s.c: Since the action of wiping off the dust from one’s feet was a symbolic act of denunciation, it may be necessary in some languages to translate this expression in ⟦Luke 10:11|Luke 10:11⟧ as ‘we wipe off as a way of denouncing you’ or ‘we wipe off as a way of showing how bad you are.’

s.dp: Case › Agent in a Causative Role Marked by Verbs
s.d: a marker of a causative relation, with the implication of something deserved
s.g: to cause; to show; to assign to

s.dp: Activities Involving Liquids or Masses › Use of Liquids
s.d: to wash off a part of the body
s.g: to wash off; to wash

s.d: to fall from a particular point or location
s.g: to fall; to fall from; to fall off

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Hold a Wrong View, Be Mistaken
s.d: to cause someone to definitely go astray in one’s beliefs or views{N:001}
s.g: to deceive; to mislead; to cause to have completely wrong views

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: to no longer believe what is true, but to start believing what is false{N:002}
s.g: to stray from the truth; to wander from the truth; to go astray from
s.c: Though in some languages one can preserve the figurative meaning of ‘to wander’ or ‘to go astray’ in connection with truth, it is not possible to do so in many languages, and therefore it may be necessary to spell out in some detail precisely what is involved, for example, ‘to stop believing what is true and to start believing what is false.’

s.d: to sail away from a point
s.g: to sail away; to sail from

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: (figurative extension of meaning employing the base {L:πνίγω<SDBG:πνίγω:000000>}[a] ‘to choke,’ {D:19.53}) to cause the death of plants by other plants crowding them out and/or overshadowing them{N:001}
s.g: to cause plants to die

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: to die as the result of drowning{N:002}
s.g: to drown

s.d: to be in perplexity, with the implication of serious anxiety
s.g: to be at a loss; to be uncertain; to be anxious; to be in doubt; consternation

s.d: to be in perplexity, with the implication of serious anxiety
s.g: to be at a loss; to be uncertain; to be anxious; to be in doubt; consternation

s.d: to throw oneself off from some object (as from a ship)
s.g: to jump off; to leap overboard

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἀπορφανίζω ‘to cause to be an orphan,’ not occurring in the NT) to cause someone to be spacially separated, with the implication of additional emotional deprivation
s.g: to separate and to deprive

s.d: the shape or shade cast by an object which blocks rays of light
s.g: shadow
s.c: In a number of languages a term for ‘shadow’ has a number of very important meanings. In some instances it is regarded as a part of personality which goes on to the next world, since a dead person no longer ‘casts a shadow.’ The shadow may also be regarded as a kind of counterpart of the personality, a type of alter ego. In cases of severe illness one may say ‘his shadow has walked away,’ and in many parts of the world the shadow of a person is an important element in the practice of black magic, for to damage a shadow may be regarded as a means of causing harm to a person.|In ⟦James 1:17|James 1:17⟧ one may translate ‘shifting shadow’ as ‘a shadow which constantly changes.’

s.d: to pull or draw away from or out of
s.g: to pull out; to draw out; to drag

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: (figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἀποσπάω<SDBG:ἀποσπάω:000000>}[a] ‘to pull out, to drag,’ {D:15.214}) to cause a change of belief so as to correspond more with the beliefs of the person or factor causing the change
s.g: to draw away; to lead away; to lure away to

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to draw oneself away from, suggesting that the movement was not sudden
s.g: to leave; to go off; to withdraw

s.d: to rise up in open defiance of authority, with the presumed intention to overthrow it or to act in complete opposition to its demands{N:001}
s.g: to rebel against; to revolt; to engage in insurrection; rebellion
s.c: It is also possible that ἀποστασία differs slightly in meaning from ἐπίστασις by virtue of the differences in prefixal formation, but there is insufficient contextual evidence to support such a view.

s.d: a written statement prepared by a husband and given to a wife as evidence of a legal divorce{N:001}
s.g: written notice of divorce

s.d: to take the roof off of a house
s.g: to remove the roof; to unroof
s.c: In ⟦Mark 2:4|Mark 2:4⟧ ἀποστεγάζω refers to only a part of the roof, and therefore in a number of languages it may be necessary to translate as ‘they made a hole in the roof.’ In view of the type of houses built in Palestine in NT times, the roof no doubt would have been flat, held up by heavy beams over which were laid planks or sticks and then covered with sun-baked clay.

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to cause someone to depart for a particular purpose
s.g: to send

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to send a message, presumably by someone{N:001}
s.g: to send a message; to send word

s.d: (an idiom, literally: to send a sickle) to begin to harvest a crop by cutting ripe grain with a sickle
s.g: to use a sickle; to swing a sickle; to begin to harvest

s.d: to take something from someone by means of deception or trickery
s.g: to defraud; to deprive by deception

s.d: to cause someone not to possess something
s.g: to deprive of
s.c: Though the resulting state of ἀποστερέω may be the mere absence of something, nevertheless the implication is that some activity has taken place to cause a person no longer to possess something. This meaning may then be expressed in some languages as to have something taken away from someone.

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Pay, Price, Cost
s.d: to not pay someone for what is owed
s.g: to withhold payment; to not pay

s.d: the role of one who has been commissioned and sent as a special messenger
s.g: apostleship; to be an apostle; to be a special messenger
s.c: See also ἀπόστολος (LN 53.74).

s.d: one who fulfills the role of being a special messenger (generally restricted to the immediate followers of Jesus Christ, but also extended, as in the case of Paul, to other early Christians active in proclaiming the message of the gospel)
s.g: apostle; special messenger
s.c: The relationship of an apostle to Jesus Christ is sometimes expressed as ‘being Christ’s messenger’ or ‘being a special messenger of Jesus Christ.’ In such a phrase, the term ‘special’ refers to having been commissioned by Jesus Christ for a particular task or role.

s.d: (derivative of {L:ἀποστέλλω<SDBG:ἀποστέλλω:000001>}[b] ‘to send a message,’ {D:15.67}) one who is sent with a message{N:001}
s.g: messenger

s.d: to question someone with hostile intent
s.g: to ask hostile questions; to inquire with hostility

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: to cause someone to turn away from a previous belief
s.g: to cause to turn away from; to cause to change one’s belief; to mislead
s.c: For another interpretation of ἀποστρέφω in ⟦Acts 3:26|Acts 3:26⟧, see LN 68.44. For another interpretation of ἀποστρέφω in ⟦Luke 23:14|Luke 23:14⟧, see LN 88.264.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Licentiousness, Perversion
s.d: to cause someone to depart from correct behavior and thus engage in serious wrongdoing
s.g: to lead astray; to pervert; to mislead
s.c: For another interpretation of ἀποστρέφω in ⟦Luke 23:14|Luke 23:14⟧, see LN 31.70.

s.d: to cause something to be in a place where it was formerly
s.g: to return; to put back

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Change of State
s.d: to cause something to turn into or to become something else or to become removed from something or someone
s.g: to change; to turn into; to remove from

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἀποστρέφω ‘to cause to turn back from,’ not occurring in the NT) to cease doing something, with the implication of rejection
s.g: to stop; to cease; to reject
s.c: For another interpretation of ἀποστρέφω in ⟦Acts 3:26|Acts 3:26⟧, see LN 31.70.

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: to no longer continue to believe as one has and hence to turn away from or to reject a previous set of beliefs
s.g: to turn away from; to reject

s.d: to abandon a former relationship or association, or to dissociate (a type of reversal of beginning to associate){N:001}
s.g: to fall away; to forsake; to turn away

s.d: to refuse to provide help to someone
s.g: to refuse to help

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Hate, Hateful
s.d: to have a strong dislike for someone or something, implying repulsion and desire for avoidance
s.g: to hate; to despise

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Religious
s.d: a state of having been excommunicated from membership in a synagogue
s.g: expelled from the synagogue
s.c: In rendering ⟦John 9:22|John 9:22⟧ it is important to indicate clearly that this is not a matter of an individual merely being forced outside of a synagogue building, but excluded from membership and thus from worship in the synagogue. In some languages this is made explicit by saying ‘his name will be erased from the list of those belonging to the synagogue’ or ‘he will no longer be able to enter a synagogue’ or ‘he will be rejected as a member of the synagogue.’

s.d: to employ formalized expressions appropriate to leaving or saying farewell to someone, possibly involving the communication of final arrangements for leaving
s.g: to say goodbye

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to say goodbye and to leave
s.g: to take leave of; to say goodbye
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘to take leave of’ or ‘saying goodbye’ is highly idiomatic, for example, ‘to snap fingers as one leaves,’ ‘to raise one’s hands together,’ ‘to clasp one’s hands before leaving,’ or ‘to bow to one another as one leaves.’

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Take, Obtain, Gain, Lose
s.d: to willingly give up or set aside what one possesses
s.g: to give up; to part with one’s possessions

s.d: to bring an activity to a successful finish{N:001}
s.g: to complete; to finish; to end; to accomplish
s.c: It is also possible to translate ἀποτελέω in ⟦Luke 13:32|Luke 13:32⟧ as ‘am performing,’ but the focus evidently is upon the completion of a series of such healings. The final phrase of ⟦Luke 13:32|Luke 13:32⟧, καὶ τῇ τρίτω τελειοῦμαι ‘and on the third day I will be finished,’ points to a possible distinction between ἀποτελέω and τελειόω, in which the first apparently serves to mark the end of a particular series, while the second points to the completion of anything and everything involved.

s.d: to put or take something away from its normal location{N:001}
s.g: to put away; to put out of the way; to remove
s.c: In ⟦Matthew 14:3|Matthew 14:3⟧ the semantic element of ‘out of the way’ is implied in the activity of ‘putting in prison.’

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἀποτίθημι<SDBG:ἀποτίθημι:000000>}[a] ‘to put away,’ {D:85.44}) to cease doing what one is accustomed to doing
s.g: to stop; to cease

s.d: to shake something out or off, in order to get rid of an object or a substance
s.g: to shake off; to shake out; to shake from
s.c: In a number of languages quite different terms for shaking will be required for the contexts of ⟦Acts 28:5|Acts 28:5⟧ and ⟦Luke 9:5|Luke 9:5⟧, since in the first instance it is an animate being which clings, and in the second instance it is simply a substance that adheres.|In a number of languages, however, the symbolic meaning of ‘shaking dust off one’s feet’ is not at all clear, so that it may be necessary to add a type of classifier to indicate that such an action symbolizes the breaking off of association. It is for this reason that the expression ἐκτιναξάμενος τὰ ἱμάτια in ⟦Acts 18:6|Acts 18:6⟧ is often translated as ‘he protested by shaking the dust from his clothes.’

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Pay, Price, Cost
s.d: (a technical, legal term) to pay compensation for damages or costs
s.g: to pay back; to remunerate
s.c: It is also possible to translate this expression in ⟦Philemon 1:19|Philemon 1:19⟧ as ‘I will pay you for any loss which you have had.’

s.d: to be particularly bold or daring in what one does
s.g: to be very bold; to be very daring

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Kindness, Harshness
s.d: to act harshly toward someone
s.g: to show harshness; to act harshly; to be harsh; harshness

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Kindness, Harshness
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἀποτομία<SDBG:ἀποτομία:000000>} ‘to show harshness,’ {D:88.73}) pertaining to acting or dealing harshly with someone
s.g: harshly
s.c: In some languages the equivalent of ἀποτομία (LN 88.73) or ἀποτόμως is a negative expression combined with showing kindness, and therefore one may translate ‘to refuse to show kindness.’ In a number of circumstances, however, the equivalent of ἀποτομία or ἀποτόμως is a highly idiomatic expression, for example, ‘to refuse to look at,’ ‘to frown upon,’ or ‘to push aside.’

s.d: purposely to avoid association with someone{N:001}
s.g: to shun; to avoid; to keep away from; to have nothing to do with

s.d: to lead or take away from a particular point

s.d: to cause a load to be carried off

s.d: the activity of using up something

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to move away from, with emphasis upon separation and possible lack of concern for what has been left
s.g: to go away; to depart; to leave

s.d: to move away from a normal location, with the implication of disappearing
s.g: to move away; to disappear
s.c: It would be difficult to translate ἀποχωρίζομαι in ⟦Revelation 6:14|Revelation 6:14⟧ as meaning literally ‘to go away,’ for this would seem strange in a reference to the sky. If, however, one employs an expression meaning to disappear, it may be necessary to say literally ‘could no longer be seen.’ For another interpretation of ἀποχωρίζομαι in ⟦Revelation 6:14|Revelation 6:14⟧, see LN 63.30.

s.d: to separate more or less definitively one from another (evidently somewhat more emphatic in meaning than {L:χωρίζω<SDBG:χωρίζω:000000>}[a] ‘to separate,’ {D:63.29})
s.g: to separate definitely; to go one’s own way; to split up
s.c: For another interpretation of ἀποχωρίζομαι in ⟦Revelation 6:14|Revelation 6:14⟧, see ἀποχωρίζομαι LN 15.14.

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sickness, Disease, Weakness
s.d: to lose one’s consciousness temporarily
s.g: to faint
s.c: It is possible that ἀποψύχω in ⟦Luke 21:26|Luke 21:26⟧ refers primarily to a psychological experience rather than a physiological one. Some scholars, however, have interpreted ἀποψύχω in this context as meaning ‘to die.’ For another interpretation of ἀποψύχω in ⟦Luke 21:26|Luke 21:26⟧, see ἀποψύχω LN 25.293.

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἀποψύχω<SDBG:ἀποψύχω:000000>}[a] ‘to faint,’ {D:23.184}) to become totally disheartened and thus ready to give up
s.g: to be totally disheartened; to be completely discouraged; to lose heart
s.c: For another interpretation of ἀποψύχω in ⟦Luke 21:26|Luke 21:26⟧, see ἀποψύχω LN 23.184.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a market town south of Rome
s.g: Forum of Appius

s.d: pertaining to not being capable of being approached
s.g: unapproachable; that which cannot be approached
s.c: It may be necessary to indicate, either in the text or in a marginal note, the reason why the light cannot be approached, for one could interpret this passage to mean that the light was either so small as not to be generally visible or so far away that it could not be reached. If, however, one uses a term for ‘light’ which implies extreme intensity of light, then the context should indicate the basis for its being unapproachable.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sin, Wrongdoing, Guilt
s.d: pertaining to being blameless in view of not having given offense
s.g: blameless; without blame
s.c: In a number of languages the concept of ‘being blameless’ as in LN 88.317 and LN 88.318 can only be expressed by a verbal expression involving some measure of complaint. For example, the expression in ⟦Acts 24:16|Acts 24:16⟧ may be rendered as ‘I do my best to live in such a way that neither God nor people can blame me’ or ‘… can complain against me.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Offend, Be Offended
s.d: pertaining to not causing offense
s.g: without causing offense; without causing trouble

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Show Favoritism, Prejudice
s.d: pertaining to behaving in an unprejudiced manner
s.g: impartially; in an impartial manner

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sin, Wrongdoing, Guilt
s.d: pertaining to not having failed to keep the law (of God)
s.g: free from stumbling; free from sinning

s.d: to cause the process of burning to begin
s.g: to ignite; to kindle; to set ablaze; to start a fire; to light a lamp
s.c: As already noted in the series of terms listed in LN 14.63, languages differ appreciably in terms employed for different phases and results of burning. For example, to set something on fire for the sake of providing warmth may be expressed by quite a different term from that which is used in speaking of the process of setting something on fire in order to destroy it.

s.d: to hold on to an object
s.g: to hold on to; to retain in the hand; to seize

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › Touch, Feel
s.d: to touch, with the implication of relatively firm contact
s.g: to touch

s.dp: Violence, Harm, Destroy, Kill › Harm, Wound

s.g: to harm

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a Christian woman, probably the wife of Philemon
s.g: Apphia

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to use force in pushing or thrusting someone or something away or aside
s.g: to push away; to thrust aside

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἀπωθέω<SDBG:ἀπωθέω:000000>}[a] ‘to push away,’ {D:15.46}) to no longer pay attention to previous beliefs
s.g: to refuse to listen to; to reject

s.d: act of destroying or causing the destruction of persons, objects, or institutions
s.g: destruction
s.c: In a number of languages it is difficult to find a general term for ‘destruction.’ What has often happened is the extension of meaning from a more specific type of reference, for example, ‘to smash,’ to a more generic meaning of ‘to destroy,’ and whether one understands the specific or more generic meaning depends largely upon the context. Accordingly, in ⟦Acts 8:3|Acts 8:3⟧ one may find a figurative usage of a term meaning ‘to smash’ (though understood in a more generic sense), for example, ‘Saul then worked in order to smash the church.’

s.d: an action demonstrating complete disregard for the value of something
s.g: waste; ruin
s.c: In the context of ⟦Mark 14:4|Mark 14:4⟧ the understanding of ἀπώλεια in the literal sense of ‘destruction’ (see LN 20.31) does not seem to be adequate. The following verse concerning the three hundred denarii would seem to indicate that it was disregard for the value of something rather than destroying the perfume. In fact, the use of the perfume would not have been a matter of destroying. Accordingly, an equivalent of ‘waste’ seems to be far more satisfactory. In some languages the equivalent of this question in ⟦Mark 14:4|Mark 14:4⟧ is ‘why did she not think about the value of the perfume?’

s.d: the content of what is expressed in a curse
s.g: curse
s.c: It may be difficult or even meaningless to speak of a person’s mouth as being ‘full of bitter curses,’ but one can often say ‘they are constantly cursing harshly’ or ‘… speaking heavy curses’ or ‘… constantly uttering harmful curses.’

s.d: a marker of result as an inference from what has preceded (frequently used in questions and in the result clause of conditional sentences)
s.g: so; then; consequently; as a result

s.d: a marker of the possibility of something being true
s.g: possible

s.d: a degree of uncertainty
s.g: perhaps

s.dp: Affirmation, Negation › Markers for a Negative Response to Questions
s.d: a marker of a negative response to questions, usually implying anxiety or impatience{N:001}
s.g: indeed; then; ever
s.c: In order to attempt to do some justice to the occurrence of the particle ἆρα, one may introduce a variety of terms which make a question somewhat more emphatically negative. In the case of ⟦Luke 18:8|Luke 18:8⟧ one might translate ‘will he indeed find faith?’ In the case of ⟦Galatians 2:17|Galatians 2:17⟧ one might translate ‘how, then, could Christ ever be a servant of sin?’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: probably a reference to the Sinai Peninsula
s.g: Arabia

s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus ({S:04000100300042}; {S:04200303300012}, apparatus)
s.g: Aram

s.g: an Arab

s.d: (derivative of {L:ἀργός<SDBG:ἀργός:000000>}[a] ‘idle, not working,’ {D:42.46}) to not be functioning
s.g: to be idle; to not be in force; to not be operative

s.d: pertaining to not working
s.g: idle; not working

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Laziness, Idleness
s.d: pertaining to habitually refusing to work (probably with a more unfavorable connotation than in the case of {L:ἄτακτος<SDBG:ἄτακτος:000000>}, {D:88.247})
s.g: lazy; good-for-nothing

s.dp: Think › To Think About, with the Implied Purpose of Responding Appropriately
s.d: pertaining to not giving careful consideration to something
s.g: careless; without thought
s.c: For another interpretation of ἀργός in ⟦Matthew 12:36|Matthew 12:36⟧, see ἀργός LN 72.21. It is also possible that ἀργός in ⟦Matthew 12:36|Matthew 12:36⟧ means useless (see ἀργός LN 65.36).

s.d: pertaining to being useless, in the sense of accomplishing nothing
s.g: useless

s.d: pertaining to showing indifference as to whether something is as it should be
s.g: careless; indifferent
s.c: It is also possible to interpret ἀργός in ⟦Matthew 12:36|Matthew 12:36⟧ as meaning ‘without thought’ (ἀργός LN 30.44), ‘worthless,’ or even ‘useless’ (ἀργός LN 65.36).

s.d: the metal silver; after gold the next most highly valued metal in the ancient world
s.g: silver
s.c: As in the case of ‘gold’ (LN 2.49), there is usually no difficulty involved in obtaining a satisfactory term for ‘silver’ in most languages. In ⟦1 Peter 1:18|1 Peter 1:18⟧, however, there is a problem in speaking of silver and gold that ‘perish,’ or even as something that can be ‘destroyed,’ since in reality one does not destroy such elements, and silver and gold do not really ‘perish.’ On the other hand, silver and gold can become oxidized and lose their value, especially if they are impure (see LN 2.60). Therefore, it seems far better to emphasize the lack of value in translating ⟦1 Peter 1:18|1 Peter 1:18⟧. A suitable rendering may then be ‘not with things that can lose their value as silver and gold.’

s.d: silver in the form of stamped coins used as money{N:001}
s.g: silver money; silver coin

s.d: (an idiom, literally: silver and gold) a generic expression for currency
s.g: money

s.d: one who makes objects out of silver (especially jewelry and fine utensils)
s.g: silversmith

s.d: the metal silver; after gold the next most highly valued metal in the ancient world
s.g: silver
s.c: As in the case of ‘gold’ (LN 2.49), there is usually no difficulty involved in obtaining a satisfactory term for ‘silver’ in most languages. In ⟦1 Peter 1:18|1 Peter 1:18⟧, however, there is a problem in speaking of silver and gold that ‘perish,’ or even as something that can be ‘destroyed,’ since in reality one does not destroy such elements, and silver and gold do not really ‘perish.’ On the other hand, silver and gold can become oxidized and lose their value, especially if they are impure (see LN 2.60). Therefore, it seems far better to emphasize the lack of value in translating ⟦1 Peter 1:18|1 Peter 1:18⟧. A suitable rendering may then be ‘not with things that can lose their value as silver and gold.’

s.d: silver in the form of stamped coins used as money{N:001}
s.g: silver money; silver coin

s.d: (derivative of {L:ἄργυρος<SDBG:ἄργυρος:000000>}[a] ‘silver,’ {D:2.51}) pertaining to being made or consisting of silver
s.g: of silver; made of silver

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: (literally: hill of Mars) the location of an Athenian court, traditionally associated with a rocky hill close to the Acropolis, though probably located in the marketplace at the foot of the hill
s.g: Areopagus
s.c: For another interpretation of Ἄρειος Πάγος in ⟦Acts 17:19|Acts 17:19⟧, ⟦Acts 17:22|Acts 17:22⟧, see Ἄρειος Πάγος LN 11.81.

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Political
s.d: an advisory council of Athens dealing with ethical, cultural, and religious matters
s.g: council of the Areopagus
s.c: It is also possible to understand τοῦ Αρείου Πάγου as referring to the location rather than to the council (see ).|It is probably wise in translating Αρειος Πάγος to simply transliterate the expression, since it has the status of a proper name. On the other hand, it is extremely important that some footnote be employed so as to indicate something of the significance of this advisory council of Athens.

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Political
s.d: a member of the council of the Areopagus
s.g: a member of the council; a member of the Areopagus

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Acceptable To, To Be Pleased With
s.d: that which causes someone to be pleased with something
s.g: means of favor; that which pleases

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Processes Involving the Mouth, Other Than Eating and Drinking
s.d: to lick an object with the tongue
s.g: to lick
s.c: It may be necessary in some languages to be somewhat more specific in the expression ‘licked his sores’ so that the text may read ‘licked the pus from his sores.’

s.d: to be or to become ready for some purpose
s.g: to be ready; to make ready; to become ready; to prepare

s.d: to cause the process of burning to begin
s.g: to ignite; to kindle; to set ablaze; to start a fire; to light a lamp
s.c: As already noted in the series of terms listed in LN 14.63, languages differ appreciably in terms employed for different phases and results of burning. For example, to set something on fire for the sake of providing warmth may be expressed by quite a different term from that which is used in speaking of the process of setting something on fire in order to destroy it.|It is possible that περιάπτω, in view of the prefix περι-, adds a component of ‘round about,’ suggesting that the blaze or fire was for the benefit of those who encircled the fire.

s.dp: Activities Involving Liquids or Masses › Use of Liquids
s.d: to wash an object which is not a body or part of a body
s.g: to wash; to clean
